title: Solving Systems of Linear Equations
student_objective: I can solve systems of two linear equations, choose an efficient method, verify the ordered-pair solution, and interpret solutions in context.
teacher_objective: Diagnose whether errors come from substitution, elimination, signed-number operations, verification, or misunderstanding the meaning of a system solution, then route targeted reteaching.

concept_cards.title: A system asks for a common solution
concept_cards.content: The solution to a system is an ordered pair that makes both equations true at the same time.

concept_cards.title: Substitution replaces an equal expression
concept_cards.content: When one equation already gives x or y in terms of the other variable, substitute that equivalent expression into the second equation.

concept_cards.title: Elimination removes one variable
concept_cards.content: Add or subtract equivalent equations so one variable cancels. Multiply an equation first when needed to create opposite coefficients.

concept_cards.title: Choose an efficient method
concept_cards.content: Use substitution when a variable is isolated or easy to isolate. Use elimination when coefficients already match or can easily become opposites.

concept_cards.title: Verify in both equations
concept_cards.content: Substitute the ordered pair into both original equations. A system solution must satisfy both, not just one.

items.prompt: Does (2, 3) satisfy both equations x + y = 5 and 2x + y = 7? Answer yes or no.
items.tutor_behavior: Substitute x = 2 and y = 3 into each equation separately.
Subtract x from both sides and preserve equality.

items.prompt: Solve y = x + 1 and x + y = 7 by substitution.
items.tutor_behavior: Replace y in the second equation with x + 1, solve for x, then back-substitute.

solution_steps.explanation: The ordered pair satisfies both equations.

items.prompt: Solve x + y = 9 and x - y = 1 by elimination.
items.tutor_behavior: Add the equations so y cancels, solve for x, then substitute back.

solution_steps.explanation: Substitute x = 5 into an original equation.

items.prompt: Solve 2x + y = 8 and 3x - y = 7 by elimination.
items.tutor_behavior: Add the equations carefully; opposite y coefficients cancel.

solution_steps.explanation: Add the equations to eliminate y.
Solve and verify in the second equation.

items.tutor_behavior: Ask what expression should replace y before revealing later steps.
Ask which variable can be eliminated by subtracting the equations.

solution_steps.explanation: Subtract the second equation from the first; the x terms cancel.
Substitute y = 2 into the second equation.

items.tutor_behavior: Score the first attempt and identify the first incorrect elimination or substitution step.
Track signed-number operations carefully when equations are combined.

items.prompt: Solve y = x + 2 and x + y = 10.
items.tutor_behavior: Use substitution and verify the ordered pair.

items.prompt: Solve x + y = 8 and x - y = 4.

items.tutor_behavior: Combine equations carefully and verify both coordinates.

items.prompt: A theater sold 20 tickets. Adult tickets cost $8 and student tickets cost $5. Total sales were $130. How many adult and student tickets were sold? Answer as adult = __, student = __.
items.tutor_behavior: Define variables, write a count equation and a revenue equation, then solve the system.

items.prompt: A student says (3, 4) solves a system because it makes the first equation true. What else must be checked?
items.answer_key: It must also satisfy the second equation.
items.explanation_prompt: Explain why a solution to a system must satisfy both equations.
items.explanation_guidance: Explain that the ordered pair is a common solution only when it makes both equations true.
items.tutor_behavior: Require reasoning about the intersection/common-solution meaning.

isolate_for_substitution.teacher_signal: Cannot isolate a variable before substitution

elimination.teacher_signal: Incorrect equation combination or variable cancellation

system_solution_meaning.teacher_signal: Treats a point satisfying only one equation as a system solution

system_modeling.teacher_signal: Incorrect variables or equations for a real-world system
